title: Doubled-word comparison run
statement: Let $P$ be a register program with oracle, let $r$ be a register, and let $j_{D1},j_{D2F},j_{D2T}$ and $j_{RB}(b)$ be states. Suppose the ordinary transitions at these states are respectively the specified first comparison action, the second comparison action for a false or true comparison bit, and the corresponding return action; suppose none of these states is a call state. Let $c$ be a configuration whose register $r$ stores the word $w_r$ from cell $0$, and let $w_i,q_0$ be a bit word and a natural number such that $q_0+2|w_i|+2\le |x|+1$ and the input symbols at positions $q_0+k$ agree, for every $k<2|w_i|+2$, with the $k$th symbol of the doubled word $\operatorname{dbl}(w_i)$ followed by $01$. For every decomposition $w_i=p u_1$, $w_r=p u_2$ and input-head position $ip$ with $ip=q_0+|p|$, there are natural numbers $T,k$ and an input-head position $ip_k$ such that $|p|\le k\le |w_r|$, and the run from state $j_{D1}$, head position $ip$, and register head at $|p|$ ends after $T$ steps in state $j_{RB}(\mathbf 1_{w_i=w_r})$, at input position $ip_k$ and register-head position $k-1$. At each earlier time $t<T$, it is in some state $s$ that is not a call state, with register-head position $q$ satisfying $0\le q\le |w_r|$.
hypotheses_covered: The transition rule at $j_{D1}$ for every input and work-tape reading
The transition rules at $j_{D2F}$ and $j_{D2T}$ for every input and work-tape reading
The transition rule at each $j_{RB}(b)$ for every input and work-tape reading
These five states are not call states
The words $w_i$ and $w_r$, and the position $q_0$
Agreement of the input with $\operatorname{dbl}(w_i)01$ on the stated positions
